headline: Reproducible tools for repeat genotyping, editing readouts, and federated variant sharing
label: Reproducible Omics Tooling Infrastructure
summary: Multi-platform long-read sequencing and federated rare-disease data sharing now demand reproducible, interoperable software beyond single analysis steps.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reproducible software infrastructure extending genomic analysis into cross-platform genotyping, editing readouts, federated sharing, and runtime state management. STRmie-HD provides alignment-free HTT CAG/CCG repeat genotyping and somatic mosaicism profiling across Illumina, PacBio, and Nanopore data. ALPINE offers a scalable, reproducible long-read amplicon pipeline that classifies CRISPR editing outcomes, including viral vector integrations and ITRs. WiNGS-API, a published federated platform, enables privacy-compliant variant-level sharing across seven centers for classification and gene discovery in rare disease. The Karolinska 10-year report, also published, addresses clinical implementation of rare-disease genome sequencing. AADT, available only as a preprint, proposes an OpenClaw agent framework that keeps patient digital twins synchronized with phenotype and variant-database updates. What is new is the layering of configurable, federated, and agent-orchestrated components rather than novel analysis algorithms, and AADT should be read as a framework-level proposal.
